title: prompt heterogeneity fuzzer and token sparsity heatmap
author: Anika Patel
description:
Motivation: Real production traffic shows wide prompt heterogeneity (short system prompts, multi-turn context dumps, long instruction documents). Existing workload generators were biased towards uniform prompt lengths and synthetic templates which under-represent token-sparsity scenarios where many prompts return very short responses. This PR adds a fuzzing harness that synthesizes realistic prompt mixes (templated, free-form, instruction-heavy, data-blobs) and an offline heatmap exporter that visualizes token-sparsity by prompt bucket to guide batching and KV-cache sizing.

What this PR does: - adds a prompt heterogeneity fuzzer that samples from a configurable catalog of prompt shapes and semantic densities; - computes a per-bucket "sparsity score" (expected response tokens / prompt tokens) and emits a two-dimensional histogram (prompt-shape x expected-response-length); - integrates a KV-cache memory probe to correlate sparsity with cache occupancy and spill events; - provides a heatmap exporter (SVG/CSV) and an opt-in CLI to generate reports for runs.

Checklist: - [x] implement fuzz harness and catalog loader - [x] add heatmap exporter and sample visual templates - [x] unit tests for sparsity scoring logic - [x] CI bench integration job and basic smoke run - [x] docs: bench-notes and usage examples

Design notes: The fuzzer is seedable and designed to be deterministic for a given catalog + seed so runs are reproducible. Prompt catalog format is YAML; each entry includes distribution parameters (length, lexical density, instruction vs data, anchor tokens). The sparsity score intentionally uses a robust trimmed-mean estimator to avoid outlier influence when a few requests generate extremely long responses. The KV-cache probe hooks into the runtime test harness via the bench telemetry API and records per-request cache hits, approximate bytes used, and any eviction counts.

Backwards compatibility: All new modules are opt-in via benchmark configs; no runtime behavior changes for existing suites unless explicitly enabled.

How to run locally: `python -m benchlab.hetero_fuzzer --catalog=benchmarks/prompt_catalog.yaml --seed=42 --out=reports/run-20241106` then `benchlab-heatmap reports/run-20241106/sparsity.csv --out=reports/heatmap.svg`.

Why this is different from previous workload runners: Instead of focusing only on sequence length distributions, this harness models semantic prompt types and their expected reply sparsity to identify batching and cache inefficiencies that only appear under mixed prompt workloads.

Related: ENG-1286 (bench strategy), PM-342 (prompt analytics).

b2d8e7f: implement sparsity scoring, KV-cache probe and unit tests
c3f4a1b: heatmap exporter, CLI and docs; fix race in cache probe; CI job updates
review_thread: Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): This is a great addition — can you explain why you chose trimmed-mean vs median for sparsity?
Anika Patel (author): Trimmed-mean preserves more signal than median for moderately skewed distributions; included tests comparing both approaches (see test_sparsity_scoring).
Daniel Kim (reviewer): KV probe looks fine but I saw a potential race in the eviction counter when runs overlap — please add a lock or use atomics.
Anika Patel (author): Addressed in c3f4a1b, switched to atomic increment via bench telemetry helper and added integration test to reproduce overlap.
Marco Ruiz (approver): CI flaky on initial run (bench job timeout). Reran and green; approving after doc addition.
release_notes: Adds a prompt heterogeneity fuzzing harness and token-sparsity heatmap exporter to help identify batching and KV-cache inefficiencies for mixed prompt workloads. Opt-in bench modules; no runtime changes by default.
notes_for_ops: When enabling this in CI, give the bench job a 40m timeout and enable the `bench_heatmap` artifact upload. Heatmap SVGs are generated under reports/<run>/heatmap.svg.
